result.title: MemMend: A Selective Revision Framework for Memory Question Answering
result.summary: Revising every answer from a long-term memory can consume substantial inference budget and damage facts that were already correct. We introduce MemMend, a modular selective revision framework that routes potentially incomplete answers to an editor, represents corrections as bounded exact-text replacements, and accepts only edits with resolvable source coordinates and valid edit operations. The editor preserves the current answer when no legal repair is proposed; accepted edits require no additional semantic-verification call. On 1,986 LoCoMo development questions, MemMend achieves 67.17 conversation-macro F1 and 88.35 mean Judge score, improving over a verified revision chain by 0.82 and 1.24 points while using 62.37% fewer revision calls. Routing uses 54.15% fewer revision calls than ungated local review, with similar F1 but a 0.67-point lower Judge score. Applied directly to native PropMem, Mem0, and SimpleMem answers, the editing interface raises F1 by 3.79, 6.44, and 0.42 points. It outperforms same-gate rewriting and saves 49.85-83.72% of editing calls relative to ungated editing, which retains higher F1 in this adaptation. A source-by-editing factorial supports local editing for F1 but leaves an independent quality benefit from source obligations unresolved. Transfer to 451 LongMemEval-V2 Small questions also favors revision efficiency, while an external PerLTQA dialogue subset reveals a completeness gap. These results support selective editing as a reusable quality-cost operating point.

AI.brief_summary: MemMend 提出模块化的选择性修订框架：先用路由器判断长时记忆问答的答案是否可能不完整，只把可疑答案交给编辑器，并以带可解析来源坐标的有界精确文本替换作为接受条件，从而在 LoCoMo 等基准上以更少的修订调用维持或提升答案质量。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「是否触发修订」的门控与来源约束、编辑成本核算，可能为 LVR 中 THINK/STOP 的收益—成本权衡与证据筛选提供可核查的方法线索，但本文是纯文本记忆问答，未涉及视觉状态或 latent 推理。
